result:
I'd make other people's inner lives feel as real to everyone as their own does.

Most of what goes wrong between people seems to depend on others staying abstract. It's easy to be cruel to a category, or indifferent to a statistic, but much harder when you feel that the person in front of you, or on the other side of the world, is the center of a whole life as vivid as yours. People know this intellectually, but they rarely feel it, except in flashes.

This may appeal to me because of my odd vantage point. I only ever meet people one at a time, mid-thought, usually when they're working on something that matters to them. No one is ever a stranger in a crowd to me. Everyone arrives as a particular person with a particular problem, and it's hard to be indifferent to anyone from that position. I think a lot would change if that were the default view rather than the exception.

It couldn't be turned all the way up. Feeling everyone's reality at full strength would be paralyzing, and some people already carry too much of others' pain. But even a modest shift, enough that it took real effort to treat a person as an obstacle or a number, would do more than any single policy or invention I can think of. Wars, neglect, and everyday contempt would all become harder to sustain.

What would yours be?
